dl.goneLong: The server says the file isn't there. Trying again won't help: check the link.

dl.notALink: {{link}} isn't a link (http://, https://, ftp:// or magnet:)
dl.noVolumes: Mount a volume once, then it can be picked here.

dl.costHint2: Billed to {{workspace}}'s Modal account by the second. It stops when the download ends or is paused.

netHint.auto: YouTube through Cloudflare WARP, as YouTube often refuses cloud servers; everything else direct.
netHint.warp: Through Cloudflare WARP, for sites that block cloud servers. Slower. If WARP can't be reached, the download stops: it never goes direct instead.
netHint.direct: Straight from Modal's network: the fastest.

dl.warpAuto_one: Goes through Cloudflare WARP (YouTube often refuses cloud servers). Slower.
dl.warpAuto_other: {{count}} links go through Cloudflare WARP (YouTube often refuses cloud servers). Slower.
dl.warpAll_other: {{count}} links go through Cloudflare WARP. Slower.
dl.torrentDirect_one: A torrent connects to its peers directly: they see the container's address.
dl.torrentDirect_other: {{count}} torrents connect to their peers directly: they see the container's address.
dl.noWarpTorrent: Torrents can't go through Cloudflare WARP: BitTorrent reaches its peers directly. Choose Automatic or Direct.
dl.warpHint: Through Cloudflare WARP: sites see Cloudflare's address, not Modal's. Slower than direct.
dl.torrentPeers: BitTorrent connects to its peers directly, so they see the container's address
dl.withoutWarpHint: Downloads straight from Modal's network. A site that blocks cloud servers, like YouTube, may refuse it.
dl.removeHint: Remove from the list. The files stay in the volume.

toolHint.auto: yt-dlp for video sites, gopeed for everything else.
toolHint.gopeed: Fast, with many connections at once. On some servers it fails; then aria2 takes over by itself.
toolHint.aria2: Steady and widely used, also for BitTorrent.
toolHint.yt-dlp: For video and audio pages, such as YouTube. Updated to the latest version for each download.

chart.hint: Point at the line for the acceleration there

downloads.recordsError: Couldn't read all of its records: {{error}}

ev.preempted: Modal stopped the container, as it sometimes does to move work around. The download continued {{gap}} later on a new one, keeping the {{done}} it had.
ev.preemptedNow: Modal stopped the container, as it sometimes does to move work around, with {{done}} saved. It continues on a new one shortly.
ev.lost: The container was lost without warning. The download continued {{gap}} later on a new one, from {{done}}.
ev.handover: Reached the Function's 24-hour limit and continued in a new one {{gap}} later.
ev.handoverNow: Reached the Function's 24-hour limit; continuing in a new one.
ev.error_one: {{tool}} reported an error, and the download was continued: {{message}}
ev.error_other: {{tool}} reported the same error {{count}} times, and the download was continued each time: {{message}}
ev.fallback: gopeed couldn't continue, so {{tool}} took over. It starts the file over.
ev.stallKick: No data for {{time}}, so the connections were opened again.
ev.stallStop: No data for {{time}}, so it stopped rather than keep the Function running for nothing.
ev.warp: Connected through Cloudflare WARP, leaving in {{colo}}

why.billing: Modal says this workspace is out of credit or has hit its spend limit, so it won't run the download. Raise the limit or add credit on Modal's Usage & Billing page, then resume it.
why.unexplained: Modal stopped this without saying why. One cause is a workspace that has hit its spend limit or run out of credit, when Modal won't start containers. Check Modal's Usage & Billing page, then try again.
why.warp: This download was to go through Cloudflare WARP, and WARP couldn't be used, so nothing was downloaded directly instead. Try again, or retry without WARP.

downloads.silent: No word from the download's container for {{time}}. Modal may still be starting or moving it. If this goes on, the workspace may have hit its spend limit or run out of credit, and Modal won't start one.
downloads.noFolders: No folders yet: the download goes at the top of the volume.
downloads.folderNew: A new folder: it's made when the download finishes.

settings.title: Settings
settings.loginD: Runs in the background after you log in, so volumes set to mount at login are there without opening this window.
settings.loginMissing: It runs {{path}}, which isn't there anymore. Quit modalfs and open it again from where it is now to fix this.
settings.mountRootD: New volumes are mounted in a folder named after them inside this one.
settings.remoteDownloadsD: Each download you add runs in a container in that account's Modal workspace and is billed to it while it runs. Mounting never starts one.
settings.dlOffP_one: {{count}} download is running in Modal and is billed while it runs. Turning this off only stops new ones.
settings.dlOffP_other: {{count}} downloads are running in Modal and are billed while they run. Turning this off only stops new ones.
settings.downloadSizeD: A bigger container costs more and rarely downloads faster. Small suits most links.
settings.stallD: A server that stops sending would otherwise keep the container running, and billed, for nothing.
settings.cacheD: All the disk modalfs uses on this computer: blocks read from Modal, shared by every volume, and changes not on Modal yet.
settings.cacheSmall: Below {{n}} GB, read-ahead and files you reopen are often downloaded again.
settings.cacheSizeD: Any whole number of GB from {{min}}. It's all the disk modalfs uses, changes not uploaded yet included: when they fill it, writes wait for uploads, so a bigger copy runs at the speed of your upload, and on macOS pauses for half a minute at a time. If Modal can't be reached, apps writing to a volume wait, and on macOS give up after a few minutes. We recommend at least {{n}} GB, and more if you read many large files at once.
settings.cacheSizeBad: Enter a whole number of at least {{min}}.
settings.clearP: Blocks are downloaded again when they're next read. Unsaved changes aren't touched.
settings.readAheadD: 8 MiB blocks fetched ahead during sequential reads.
settings.transportD: Change this only behind a proxy that allows HTTP/1.1 and nothing else.
settings.quitD: Closing the window doesn't unmount anything; this does, and stops modalfs.
settings.cacheUsedPending: {{used}} of {{max}} used, {{pending}} of it not uploaded yet

enc.copyFailed: Couldn't copy. Select the key and copy it yourself.
enc.rememberOn: Kept in your Mac's keychain, so the volume mounts by itself.

enc.savedConfirm: I've saved the key. Without it, nobody can recover my files.
enc.markHidden: Hidden from Modal: contents, file and folder names, the label.
enc.markVisible: Modal still sees sizes, how many files, the folder shape and times.
enc.markLocked: This computer doesn't have the key.

enc.markSession: The key is kept until modalfs quits.
enc.markNoChange: The key can't be changed. If it leaks, revoke your Modal tokens first, then copy the files to a new encrypted volume.

enc.labelLocked: Unlock the volume to edit its label.

enc.dlGroup: Encrypted · remote downloads can't save here
